mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate directly lowers the risk-free rate, reducing the discount rate applied to equity cash flows and generating positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS below 1.5% in 60% of periods and average 20-day return is negative with t-test p-value > 0.05 for mean return > 0.

mechanism_narrative: A rising unemployment rate exceeding 4.0% signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which typically precedes reduced consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: UNRATE > 4.0% and average 20-day return is positive with t-test p-value < 0.05 for mean return > 0 over any 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in housing starts and real personal consumption expenditures signal robust consumer demand, supporting corporate earnings growth and generating positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: HOUST and RSAFS both rising in >40% of periods and average 20-day return is negative with t-test p-value > 0.05 for mean return > 0.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production below 100 signals weakening manufacturing output, which typically precedes reduced corporate profitability and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: INDPRO < 100 and average 20-day return is positive with t-test p-value < 0.05 for mean return > 0 over any 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: Higher inflation (CPIAUCSL above 2.5% annualized) typically triggers central bank tightening, increasing real interest rates and compressing equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: CPIAUCSL inflation rate > 2.5% and average 5-day return is positive with t-test p-value < 0.05 for mean return > 0 over any 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A slowdown in job growth (PAYEMS growth rate below 0.1%) signals weakening labor market conditions, which typically precedes reduced consumer spending and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: PAYEMS growth rate < 0.1% and average 60-day return is positive with t-test p-value < 0.05 for mean return > 0 over any 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in inflation (CPIAUCSL inflation rate > 2.5%) and federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS > 1.5%) signal active monetary tightening, which typically compresses equity valuations and generates negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: CPIAUCSL inflation rate > 2.5% and FEDFUNDS > 1.5% and average 20-day return is positive with t-test p-value < 0.05 for mean return > 0 over any 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: Strong job growth (PAYEMS growth rate above 0.2%) signals a tight labor market, which typically supports consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: PAYEMS growth rate > 0.2% and average 5-day return is negative with t-test p-value > 0.05 for mean return > 0 over any 3-year window.
